translations.text: This day's service and the celebration of this season speak about God's coming. This season until midwinter is called Adventus Domini, that is, the Lord's coming.
His coming is his incarnation. He came to us when he joined our nature to his almighty Godhead, so that he might set us free from the devil's power.
Now the custom stands in God's church that all God's servants, in the church services, both in holy readings and in joyful hymns, continually recite the songs of the prophets during this season.
The prophets, through God's Spirit, prophesied Christ's coming in human nature, and wrote many books about it,
which we now read through at God's service before his birth-feast, in his honour, because he was willing to visit us so mercifully.

Christ came visibly to mankind at that time, but he is always invisibly with his chosen servants, just as he himself promised, saying thus: "Behold, I am with you all days, until the end of this world."
With these words he made clear that there will always be, until the ending of the world, people chosen by him, who are worthy to have God dwelling with them.
The holy prophets prophesied both the first coming at the birth and also the second coming at the great judgement.
We also, God's servants, strengthen our faith with the services of this season, because in our hymns we confess our redemption through his first coming,
and we urge ourselves to be ready for his second coming, so that we may follow him from the judgment to eternal life, as he promised us.
About the celebration of this season the apostle Paul spoke in this epistle reading to the people of Rome, and also to all believing people:
exhorting thus: "My brothers, know that it is now time for us to rise from sleep: our salvation is nearer than when we believed.
The night has passed, and the day has drawn near. Let us cast off the works of darkness and be clothed with the weapons of light, so that we may walk honourably in the day;
not in gluttony and drunkenness, not in adulterous beds and impurity, not in strife and envy; but be clothed through the Lord Jesus Christ."
The apostle has roused us, so that at some time we should rise from the sleep of our sloth and unbelief, as you heard in this present reading:
"My brothers, know that it is now time for us to rise from sleep."
Truly it is not fitting for us to be always soft in our faith, like tender little children; rather we must hasten toward perfect maturity by keeping God's commandments.
We must shake off that sluggish sleep from us, and abandon the devil's works, and walk in the light, that is, in good works.
Long ago the light of knowledge shone throughout the circle of the earth, and very many shine on the way of truth, who travel by the path of the gospel to the joy of eternal life.
Truly now "our salvation is nearer than when we believed." Through growing understanding and good will, salvation is nearer to each person than it was when he first believed,
and therefore he must always grow in daily diligence, as the psalmist said of God's chosen ones: "The saints go from strength to strength."
Also each person's last day comes nearer and nearer; and the general judgment draws closer day by day, at which each one will receive according to what he earned in the body, whether good or evil.
Let us therefore flee every evil and do good as far as we are able, lest we wish to do so when we cannot, and ask for more time when death compels us to depart.
"The night has passed, and the day has drawn near." Here the apostle used "night" for the old ignorance that reigned throughout the whole world before Christ's coming;
but he shattered that erring ignorance through the illumination of his presence, just as the bright day drives away the dim darkness of the black night.
The devil is also called night, and Christ day, who mercifully set us free from the devil's darkness and gave us the light of understanding and truth.
"Let us cast off the works of darkness and be clothed with the weapons of light, so that we may walk honourably in the day."
Let us cast off our past evils through confession and repentance, and let us from now on firmly resist the devil's temptations,
as the same apostle urged those under his care in another place: "Resist the devil, and he will flee from you; draw near to God, and he will draw near to you."
The weapons of light are the works of righteousness and truth. We must be clothed with these weapons, so that we may walk honourably in the day.
Just as the light of day prevents anyone from doing what the night permits, so also the knowledge of truth, that is, the thought of our Lord's will, does not permit us to commit wicked deeds.

We are always seen by God, both outwardly and inwardly; therefore everyone who does not wish to be condemned must take every care not to transgress God's commandments: not in gluttony and drunkenness.
We should have spiritual feasting, as the same apostle taught in these words: "When you gather together for a meal, let each of you have wholesome teaching in his mouth and a psalter in his hand."
Drunkenness is a deadly thing, and the fuel of lust. Solomon said, "Nothing is secret where drunkenness reigns."
In another place the same apostle lamented the life of intemperate people, saying, "Their belly is their god, and their end is destruction, and their glory is in their shame."
Not in adulterous beds and in impurities; rather, let there be honourable marriage among believers, so that no fornication or impurity is even named in God's church. Not in strife and envy.

Christ said of peaceable people that they are called the children of God, and truly the quarrelsome are the devil's limbs. The evil man always seeks strife, and a cruel angel will be sent against him.
Envy is a harmful vice, and the envious man always lives in turmoil, because envy blinds his mind and deprives it of all spiritual joy.
Through envy the devil deceived the first-created man, and the envious man is a partaker with the devils.
True peace drives away discord and enlightens the secret places of the mind, and truly envy multiplies anger.
The apostle closed this epistle with these words: "But be clothed through the Lord Jesus Christ."
All who are baptized in Christ are clothed with Christ, if they adorn their Christianity with works of righteousness.
The same apostle described these garments more clearly in another place, saying, "Clothe yourselves, as God's chosen ones, with mercy and with kindness,
with humility, with moderation, with patience, and above all things have true love, which is the bond of all perfection;
and let the peace of Christ rejoice in your hearts, to which you are called in one body.
Be thankful, and let God's word dwell among you abundantly, in all wisdom teaching and exhorting one another, in psalms and spiritual hymns, singing with God's grace in your hearts.
Whatever you do in word or in deed, always do it in the Lord's name, giving thanks to the Almighty Father through his Son, who dwells with him forever in the unity of the Holy Spirit."

Let us therefore prepare ourselves with these garments mentioned above, according to the apostle's exhortation, so that we may come with festive service to the wonderful feast of the birth of our Lord, to whom be glory and praise for ever and ever. Amen.
